chunks: Those who persevere seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, and repel evil with good — those will have the best outcome in the Hereafter.

key_terms.ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِمْ: Seeking the countenance/face of their Lord
key_terms.عُقْبَى الدَّارِ: The good end/outcome of the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What are the key virtues of the righteous mentioned in Surah Ar-Ra'd verse 22?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the triad of patience (sabr), prayer (salah), and charity (infaq) as the pillars of spiritual resilience, with 'repelling evil with good' (daf' al-sayyi'ah bi-l-hasanah) serving as a practical method for purifying the soul. The 'good end' (Uqba) is understood not merely as Paradise but as the ultimate success of the heart in recognizing and adhering to divine guidance, a concept deeply linked to the Ahl al-Bayt's example of steadfastness.
